high-8-562be715-105.text: The snow keeps a perfect account until the wind edits it. I travel early if I want the uncorrected story.

sun-8-6e616a69-105.text: I follow the old watchfire route once each season. The route is the same, but the country never quite is.

tamsin-4753581a-108.text: The keeper’s lantern is ready. Seek the three beacons beneath the Lantern Gate. Dawn, then Tide, then Night.

grey-3-8f04ddd6-112.text: I sew wounds with the same steadiness my mother used on sails. She says I have chosen the more difficult fabric.

reed-9-7e54bbfa-115.text: My kitchen serves the early fishing crews before sunrise. I know which boats have returned by which chairs fill up.

high-5-696837b8-116.text: We grow the quick crops under glass and the patient ones beneath straw. The mountain does not hurry. Neither can we.

mara-4b9734d0-117.text: Follow the broken lanterns from Hearthwick to the Gate. The people of the Nine Marches each hold a part of the story.

high-7-38abe309-117.text: I check the ridge markers after every storm. A missing pole can kill as surely as a broken bridge, only more quietly.

sun-10-539ae43f-118.text: I keep spare lamp wicks in my belt pouch. The grand gestures get remembered; the small preparations keep the road lit.

willow-5-499ea628-119.text: The marsh never gives you a straight boundary. I plant where the herons stand and move my fences when they move theirs.

orin-c0fc0131-120.text: These leaves will mend our neighbors. Elin, the Gate’s Warden, is my sister. Take her medallion. I will travel with you.

copper-3-3bdd7a70-121.text: Stone dust settles in a person slowly. I make the crews wash before supper, and they complain as though I invented water.

reed-8-3a878796-122.text: The fen paths move when the tide is high. I tie colored cords above the water so strangers can find the ground beneath it.

thorn-2-d8c91601-125.text: I forge pruning hooks more often than swords. A well-balanced hook feeds a household. I wish that earned the same admiration.

grey-6-584ddc23-126.text: I keep a shelf of objects left behind by travelers. If nobody returns for a year, the sale pays for a stranger’s passage home.

sun-9-ad5f3f66-126.text: I leave a map on every supper table. Strangers begin by asking for directions and often end by sharing the rest of their meal.

thorn-3-6cb89d76-127.text: I learned the plants by making a notebook of what not to use. It is longer than the book of cures, and I consult it more often.

copper-4-1a7c0fc1-129.text: A miner’s pie must survive a fall down a shaft. Mine are sturdy enough to be accused of it. The filling is better than the jokes.

salt-8-d7d6e6e6-129.text: I count footprints beyond the tide line. Bandits believe the sea washes away every trace. They forget the sand beneath the pines.

grey-4-3ece05cf-130.text: I make a different bread for every ship’s home port. Captains argue about authenticity. Their crews usually ask for another slice.

copper-10-7fba37b1-131.text: I used to sort gemstones. Watching a crowd uses the same patience: you notice what does not belong before you decide what it means.

salt-4-86bc2fe-131.text: I bake rye because wheat struggles in the coastal wind. The loaf is dark, the crust is honest, and the watch can carry it for days.

salt-7-f28c8eba-131.text: The fort taught me to obey signals. A merchant taught me that signals can be bought. These days I check who is holding the lantern.

grey-8-c5e520d9-131.text: The manor’s garden grows through its iron fence. I leave a path to the kitchen door. Haunted or not, a house should have a way out.

copper-5-8ee32cfb-132.text: My sheep graze the old slag slopes. Nothing looked capable of growing there when I arrived. Now the children call it the green hill.

salt-0-df9b2a72-132.text: Keep watch. Keep faith. That is what we tell the children, at least. A red-sailed smuggler buried a ledger beneath the coastal fort.

high-0-af5179d0-132.text: Our fuel stores are counted in nights, not logs. I ask every household what they can spare before winter asks what they can survive.

thorn-6-41279df0-132.text: My trade routes follow the old root bridges. I carry light loads and remember every repair. Speed is not the same thing as arriving.

thorn-8-19e9ff73-132.text: The hollow orchard has paths under its paths. I mark the unstable ground with woven grass and hope curiosity remembers to look down.

salt-9-b7d3f9e6-133.text: My guest book contains four languages and several drawings. Everyone gets a room, even if we have to negotiate breakfast by pointing.

willow-7-65a20b09-134.text: My boots have been wet since I joined the watch. I mark safe crossings with three stones. If you see only two, wait for a local guide.

salt-10-d774956b-134.text: I practice the warning horn every third morning. Children complain about the noise. I hope that remains their strongest opinion of it.

grey-9-9eceec2d-134.text: I learned soup from a dozen sailors and have disappointed all twelve by combining their recipes. The rest of the harbor seems pleased.

corin-9c1147af-135.text: There is a chair by my hearth for a traveler who promised to return. Until then, anybody waiting for good news is welcome to borrow it.

reed-2-9fd71d6b-135.text: Salt enters every hinge here. I mix wax into my oil and keep a little furnace burning through the damp months. The sea has not won yet.

thorn-1-d4e8a948-135.text: I study rings in fallen timber. The trees remember droughts our records call prosperous years. Somebody prospered; it was not everyone.

sun-3-6a466115-135.text: My patients bring news from every road. I do not repeat their private troubles, but I do remember which settlements need more supplies.

jory-986c2781-136.text: Galen thinks I patrol too slowly. I am learning which shutters belong to people who live alone. A watch should notice more than enemies.

willow-8-c430f665-137.text: I follow birds to find changes in the water. Last autumn the swallows refused the chapel roof. Whatever frightened them was not the rain.

copper-9-7b3536b8-137.text: The miners sing badly and loudly at my tables. I charge for spilled ale, never for the singing. Silence after a shift is what worries me.

thorn-10-2502c55d-137.text: I joined the watch to protect the harvest carts. I stayed because the road carries letters, medicine, and people who have no cart at all.

high-10-68800b94-138.text: I used to fear the mountain’s silence. Now I fear the sudden sound that does not belong in it. There is a difference you learn by staying.

copper-8-3da8da5b-139.text: I map the ledges where the quarry birds nest. Their flight tells me which walls are loosening. The foreman finally started reading my maps.

reed-3-2f9bfe4c-139.text: I keep dry blankets in three houses along the harbor road. Rescues are easier when the preparation happened before anybody needed rescuing.

wren-763f0d7-140.text: A deer path south of the cottages saved six children during the flood. I clear it every spring. Nobody has asked me to, and nobody needs to.

willow-10-1b428bc7-140.text: I learned to swim before I learned to write. My reports are brief, but nobody on my watch has had to explain the river to a grieving family.

high-6-ff8b3a20-140.text: My sled routes include homes too isolated to be profitable. Their owners repair the runners when I arrive. We have found a fair arrangement.

reed-1-460d2b81-141.text: The songs praise the barrow king for his victories. His accounts show a man selling his crown to buy seed. I would rather teach that version.

reed-10-b8e2ffb0-141.text: I took this post after my brother followed a false beacon. I check the real lamp every evening, even when someone else says they already did.

high-9-9b662615-141.text: The warmest bed in my inn stays empty for a late arrival. Losing one night’s rent is cheaper than losing the sort of place we meant to build.

salt-2-4185e09-142.text: The road shelter needs five sound beams, not a grand dedication. Give me seasoned wood and a quiet afternoon and I will make something useful.

thorn-4-ce335161-142.text: I bake with orchard fruit that is too bruised to sell. The children think the trees grow special pie apples for me. I have not corrected them.

thorn-7-b703e1ea-142.text: I patrol with a whistle carved from fallen wood. The orchard workers know its call. An alarm is useful only if people know who is sounding it.

orin-90e95283-143.text: Elin waited at the Gate for every lost traveler. She stayed so long she forgot that she was allowed to come home. Her medallion may remind her.

copper-0-5e849be5-143.text: The miners choose their own shift leaders. I record the votes and settle the arguments afterward. A town built on stone still depends on trust.

grey-10-28fc2f-143.text: I was a rope-maker before I joined the watch. I still carry a coil. Most people need pulling out of trouble more often than they need fighting.

high-2-2d22e6e7-143.text: Cold iron punishes a careless hand. I warm the tools as well as the metal, and I teach apprentices to notice when their fingers have gone numb.

thorn-9-fbbac0be-143.text: My tables were made from one fallen oak. I left its knots visible. Guests sometimes trace them while telling stories they did not mean to tell.

sun-5-6a0d2631-143.text: I plant a strip of flowers between the crop rows. It helps the bees and irritates anyone who thinks useful things should not also be beautiful.

copper-7-24f917ff-144.text: A falling stone broke my shield on my first quarry rescue. I carry the dented rim on my belt. It reminds me that the ground can be an enemy too.

reed-7-55a44adc-144.text: I can identify most ships by their rigging. The red-sailed vessel changes its name every season, but never the way its captain avoids the watch.

grey-2-4cddcbae-145.text: A ship’s fitting must be repaired before the tide turns. That is how I learned to work quickly without pretending haste is a substitute for care.

reed-5-d4ef70b1-146.text: I grow vegetables above the tide line in raised beds. Every winter somebody suggests moving farther inland. Every spring the harbor needs feeding.

salt-5-34638009-146.text: Salt grass is stubborn enough to hold these dunes together. I grow food between it and leave more wild ground than my neighbors consider sensible.

high-3-3a8f7611-146.text: I keep broth simmering through the long night. People arrive claiming they only came to deliver news. I hand them a bowl before asking which news.

sun-0-773d0352-146.text: Sunward’s motto promises an open door. I spend much of my day making sure it means something practical: a spare key, a meal, a person who answers.

ada-9f50acd4-147.text: The journal, copper coil, and archive lens are all pieces of the same story. The Gate was meant to guide travelers. Someone taught it to keep them.

copper-2-bb0cf618-147.text: Every tool leaving my forge has a small kestrel stamped under the grip. If it fails, I want the owner to know exactly who owes them an explanation.

tamsin-e3d99d9-148.text: The first blade I sold snapped at the hilt. I keep both pieces above my bench. A beautiful tool is useless if the person holding it cannot trust it.

willow-9-ccff7482-148.text: My inn has a second-floor door that once opened onto a boat. We kept it after the flood as a reminder to build for the weather you hope never comes.

reed-0-ceec1da9-149.text: We built the harbor table from a wreck’s surviving beams. Every arrival is offered a seat. The false lighthouse has left too many seats empty lately.

sun-4-fdb2d5da-149.text: I am collecting accounts of eight places beneath the Marches. Baking pays for the paper. People underestimate how much history a kitchen can support.

reed-4-975fde9f-150.text: Clove was my grandmother’s favorite spice and apparently a suitable name for a child. I put it in the festival buns so her decision still makes sense.

salt-6-d0692579-151.text: I used to carry luxury cloth on the eastern road. Now I stock needles, boots, and lamp oil. The things people miss most are rarely the things in songs.

high-0-f68be7fe-151.text: Hold the flame against the winter. That is what we tell the children, at least. The abbey beneath the glacier kept the last verse of the keeper’s oath.

sun-7-13e20e0e-151.text: The crossroads watch sees travelers at their most tired. I start with directions and a cup of water. Suspicion can wait until there is a reason for it.

thorn-0-5a2be90d-152.text: Our oldest agreements are carved into living trees. I make sure their meanings are copied before bark grows over the words. A promise needs tending too.

sun-6-e5ab6cfa-152.text: I price ordinary tools plainly and rare objects cautiously. A customer who understands the purchase is more likely to return with a story worth hearing.

willow-3-2046d1f4-153.text: I learned to make remedies in a ferryman’s cabin. Our patients included rival crews who refused to share a blanket. Fever is an excellent cure for pride.

salt-3-f3c4a984-154.text: My name invites strangers to test my patience. I have learned that mercy can include telling someone firmly to sit down and stop making their wound worse.

grey-5-df5709cd-154.text: My orchard leans away from the sea wind. I prune with the lean instead of fighting it. Trees dislike being told what a drawing says they should look like.

copper-0-bd8fe9a4-155.text: Honest iron. Unbroken promises. That is what we tell the children, at least. The quarry miners broke into a sealed vault. The stones now hum before a raid.

salt-0-7aef444d-155.text: The watchfire belongs to the whole coast. I will not let a captain buy the darkness around it. Bring me evidence, and I will make sure the harbor hears it.

grey-7-a11eed07-155.text: The harbor at night is a hundred moving reflections. I watch the gaps between them. A boat without a lamp is often more informative than a boat with three.

nell-b8a35b32-156.text: I grow beans on the ground the river took from my father. The silt is richer now. I wish improvement did not so often arrive wearing the face of a disaster.

willow-4-c2f616b7-156.text: Reed flour makes a dense loaf, so I cut it thin and toast it with honey. Dockworkers call it a brick until they smell the oven. Then they call it breakfast.

high-4-10d9f7fe-156.text: I was named Ember during a winter without enough firewood. I like to think every loaf leaving my oven proves my parents were optimistic rather than foolish.

edda-89f32833-157.text: My first shop fit inside a handcart. Now I keep the cart by the door to remind myself that a customer buying one needle may be spending everything they have.

reed-6-dddc9a06-157.text: My best ledger lists loans repaid in work: a patched roof, a repaired net, three nights watching a sick neighbor. Gold is only one way to balance an account.

sun-2-f385a93-158.text: I repair hinges for free on the first morning of spring. It began as an advertisement. Now half the town arrives with breakfast and I cannot call it business.

galen-d0cbfc42-159.text: I was a frightened watchman until an older guard made me learn every night sound on this road. Courage became easier when the darkness stopped being anonymous.

copper-6-8018052d-159.text: I weigh ore twice: once for the seller and once with the seller watching. My father called the second weighing unnecessary. His customers called it reassuring.

bram-54e3bcc2-160.text: My mother marked the first loaf with a sun so a hungry stranger would know it was theirs. I have changed her recipe three times. I have never changed that mark.

willow-6-eff15e4-162.text: I trade in waterproof things: oilcloth, sealed jars, and promises I can actually keep. The last category has the smallest profit and the most returning customers.

reed-0-fa478ef0-162.text: A safe harbor in uncertain weather. That is what we tell the children, at least. The lighthouse lens is missing. Ships follow a false light toward the salt caves.

willow-2-f886da06-163.text: Holt is a short name for a long line of boatbuilders. I became a smith because every good boat eventually needs a hinge, a nail, or an anchor nobody thought about.

copper-1-aa529742-163.text: I study the sounds that travel through the quarry. The deepest seam answers in a rhythm no hammer makes. I have written it down without pretending I understand it.

sun-1-8ecd76a3-163.text: The watchfire chart names the people who walked each road. I want the map restored because destinations matter less without the stories of how people reached them.

grey-0-d7484ef-165.text: Greyharbor receives stories faster than it receives ships. I keep a public noticebook so a rumor has to stand beside a named witness before it becomes an accusation.

thorn-5-aaef0a14-165.text: My grandmother left a silver seed for a spring she would never see. I intend to plant it, even if I cannot promise what the world will look like when it bears fruit.

orin-2f09884b-166.text: My sister Elin used to race me along the river. She always stopped for anybody who fell behind. At the Gate, that kindness became a duty she could no longer put down.

salt-1-934a345f-166.text: People expect elegant writing from a person called Quill. My handwriting is terrible. Fortunately, my maps have saved more travelers than a beautiful signature would.

willow-0-d85d3fb-168.text: What the river takes, the reeds remember. That is what we tell the children, at least. A ferryman hears bells under the water. The drowned chapel holds more than bones.

willow-1-ab882f71-169.text: I catalogued the drowned chapel from boat sketches. Each summer the water reveals another window. I am beginning to think the building is returning one memory at a time.

thorn-0-4ec4f99f-169.text: The roots bind us to one another. That is what we tell the children, at least. The orchard east of town bears silver fruit. Its caretaker vanished into the hollow roots.

willow-0-477beb25-170.text: The flood bell used to hang where the reeds are now. I organize the ferry roster by who needs to cross, rather than who can pay. It causes arguments I am willing to have.

high-1-1012746f-172.text: The abbey’s final verse is missing from every copy in town. The omission is too consistent to be an accident. I would like to hear what the keepers were afraid to remember.

grey-0-4ce4e239-173.text: A thousand stories enter by the sea. That is what we tell the children, at least. The haunted manor on the western road still sets a place for a daughter who never returned.

sun-0-523a677b-176.text: A promise is a door left open. That is what we tell the children, at least. The Sunken Archive lies beyond the eastern hills. Three beacons remember the way: Dawn, Tide, Night.

mara-47517f96-177.text: I keep the names of every household in a blue book. After the flood, I refused to erase the families whose roofs were gone. Some have come back; some still have a place waiting.

mara-510233-178.text: Every stranger deserves a light. That is what we tell the children, at least. The old mill stopped turning the night our lanterns failed. Its keeper left a journal in the cellar.

ada-f8cc71cc-195.text: Eren taught me to read a waterwheel by listening to its bearings. His last journal stopped halfway through a calculation. I can finish the machinery, if somebody can tell me what happened to him.

high-9-dd94dbce-266.text: I am Tor, Highmere's innkeeper. My usual shift is 07:00 to 21:30. My work includes serving guests at the inn, sweeping the inn’s hearth, setting the next supper table. I return to my household after my shift and the evening gathering. Right now I am seeking shelter.
